set.approach: You will not see this flow from the highway. Top out Salt and Pepper, then walk up the gully above it for about five minutes; the ice spills off the rim at its head.

wa_banks_lake_ice_climbing_climb_above_s.notes: The stored approach (the generic Banks Lake sentence: a short walk, visible from the road) is wrong for this flow - Mountain Project says it is hidden from below and reached by walking up the drainage above Salt and Pepper (a WI5) after climbing it. set.approach: The flows form high on the slope above SR 155 near milepost 22.5, in the band of cliff just below the hilltop; the walk up crosses private land, so get the owner's permission first.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Drive SR 155 to about milepost 22.5, south of Electric City; the Electric Avenue flows can be seen on the hillside above the road. Pull fully off the shoulder.

to.notes: Reaching the flows crosses private property; ask the landowner before climbing.

sql_fixes.why: Mountain Project says access crosses private property and permission is needed (it guesses a developer owns it). WA DNR's public-lands layer shows no public parcel anywhere on a 0.006 x 0.014 degree grid around SR 155 MP 22.5 (WSDOT milepost point 47.91170,-119.05936) up to the hilltop; the nearest public (Reclamation) land is the lakeshore strip from about 47.914 north. Owner unknown - do not name one.

wa_banks_lake_ice_climbing_electric_aven.notes: This route is NOT on Reclamation/WDFW or State Parks land, unlike the other Banks Lake flows. The stored approach and trailheadDirection said the flows sit between MP 8 and 17 and are a short walk - wrong for this one (MP 22.5, a climb to the hilltop band). Replaced with our own sentences. The area row's lat/lng (47.81441,-119.1536) is Mountain Project's area GPS, copied onto every route page there; it is a single highway point near SR 155 MP 14 for a crag that spans MP 8 to 22.5 - the owner may want it flagged coords_approx.
